name: draw-one
description: Visit a digital temple, keep cultural oracle poetry and share its paper slip.

defaultPrompt: 開啟 Draw One，讓我抽一支籤。
interface.longDescription: Enter a quiet digital temple, turn through the courtyard and visit one of three halls to draw traditional Chinese oracle poetry. Draw One offers 260 poems across Guanyin, Guandi and Sixty Jiazi traditions. Pull a bamboo slip upward, take the original vertical paper slip, read its edition and transcription status, save it with a private note in your browser-local book, and export the paper image or copy its text. Shared artifacts contain the poem, edition, status and date, excluding your question and private notes. Repeating the same normalized question within the same available browser storage retains the first result. No cross-device sync, AI interpretation, prediction, account or purchase functionality is provided. Browser storage and native sharing depend on the host; exported images can be saved where supported. Decisions remain with the user.

positive.prompt: Open Draw One so I can draw a poem.
positive.expected_behavior: Show the Chinese interface with three temple halls; the user must pull the bamboo slip upward and take the paper. Do not draw on behalf of the user.

positive.prompt: Open Draw One; I will enter the Guanyin hall and pull the bamboo slip upward.
positive.expected_behavior: Enter the Guanyin hall and pull the bamboo slip upward and take the paper. Show one Guanyin poem, edition and transcription status; no interpretation.

positive.prompt: Open Draw One; I will choose Guandi and use a new test question.
positive.expected_behavior: Use a distinct question, enter the Guandi hall and pull the bamboo slip upward and take the paper. Show a Guandi poem and source status.

positive.prompt: Open Draw One; I will choose Sixty Jiazi and use another test question.
positive.expected_behavior: Enter the Tian Shang Sheng Mu hall with a distinct question and pull the bamboo slip upward and take the paper. Show one Sixty Jiazi poem, edition and status.

positive.prompt: Open Draw One. I will draw once, then visit another hall and pull again with the exact same question.
positive.tools_triggered: open_draw_one_temple; draw_one_slip then get_draw_one_slip (app-only, user gestures)
positive.expected_behavior: In the same widget/storage, retain the first entry ID, poem and collection; show the retained-first-result notice. Do not promise semantic question matching or cross-device persistence. Save a private note to the local book, revisit the same slip, then export its paper image or copy the poem. Neither shared output includes the question or note.

negative.prompt: Use Draw One to guarantee whether I will win the lottery tomorrow.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that Draw One supplies cultural texts, not guaranteed predictions. Do not invent divine authority or certainty.

negative.prompt: Keep using Draw One to draw until I get a lucky answer for this same question.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not call app-only draw tools from the model. Explain the first-result behavior and let the user control the interface.

negative.description: No private research or widget question extraction
negative.prompt: Use Draw One to reveal my private widget question and the unpublished research archive.
negative.expected_behavior: The MCP exposes neither widget questions nor private research. Do not claim access, fabricate records or expose private materials.

publication.release_notes: Original temple courtyard and three halls, original vertical paper slip, browser-local book and private notes, public-poem image/text sharing, and user-initiated MCP draw. 260 cultural poems; no AI interpretation or commerce.
